question: Your team wants Claude Code to build a caching layer that reuses review results for unchanged files between pipeline runs, so repeated pushes to a pull request skip redundant reviews. Nobody on the team has designed a cache before, and a quick prototype once produced stale feedback after a dependency changed. What is the most effective way to start this implementation with Claude Code?

options.text: Give Claude two or three input/output examples of review results so that it infers the caching rules from the shown pattern.
options.reason: Concrete input/output examples clarify a transformation that prose describes inconsistently, but they do not uncover design considerations that the team has not thought of yet.

options.text: Write a detailed prose specification of the cache yourself and send every requirement to Claude together in a single message.
options.reason: A single detailed message suits interacting issues that are already known, but a team new to caching would leave out the considerations it did not anticipate, which the interview pattern would surface.

options.text: Ask Claude to implement the caching layer right away, then fix each stale-feedback problem one at a time as it appears in pipeline runs.
options.reason: This skips the step of surfacing design considerations before implementing, so the team finds gaps like invalidation only after they cause bad feedback in production runs.

options.text: Ask Claude to interview you first, raising questions about invalidation triggers and failure modes, before it writes any implementation code.
options.reason: The interview pattern has Claude ask questions that surface considerations the developer may not have anticipated, such as cache invalidation strategies and failure modes, before it implements a solution in an unfamiliar domain.
